Kofi: Morning — joining today. On macOS Ventura M2; followed the bootstrap. Homebrew in /opt/homebrew, asdf installed via brew, fish set as my shell. Terminal.app shows asdf shims, but VSCode integrated terminal (launched from Dock) has old PATH and `asdf` not found. Tried adding exports to config.fish but VSCode still picks up system PATH. Any tips?

Rina: welcome! GUI apps launched from Finder/Spotlight/Dock don't get your shell rc. Two options: (1) have VSCode launch a login shell (terminal.integrated.shellArgs.osx = ['-l']), or (2) export PATH via launchctl so the GUI inherits it: `launchctl setenv PATH /opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH` (restart VSCode). We prefer the login shell setting to avoid global launchctl envs.

Diego: +1. Also for fish ensure config.fish sets PATH early: `set -x PATH $HOME/.asdf/shims /opt/homebrew/bin $PATH` — that makes non-login shells see shims. If you use apps that spawn shells via login flag, put the asdf source in ~/.zprofile (if you also use zsh). Mixing shells can be messy.

Kofi: Tried both: setting login shell makes VSCode show asdf, but my GUI apps (Finder services) still don't get GNUPGHOME etc. I'm also hitting gpg errors with nodejs plugin: `gpg: no writable keyring found`. I run gpg via gpg2 from brew and pinentry-mac is installed. Any known fixes?

Rina: For gpg: ensure GNUPGHOME is a writable dir in your home. `export GNUPGHOME=$HOME/.gnupg-asdf && mkdir -p $GNUPGHOME && chmod 700 $GNUPGHOME` then run the import script: `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring`. If pinentry prompts fail inside VSCode, install and configure pinentry-mac and set `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` in interactive shells — but GUI terminals don't use TTY so use gpg-agent with pinentry-mac integration: `echo 'use-agent' >> $GNUPGHOME/gpg.conf` and `echo 'pinentry-program /opt/homebrew/bin/pinentry-mac' >> $GNUPGHOME/gpg-agent.conf` then `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent`.

Diego: Another subtle one: if you installed gnupg via brew but VSCode's env picks up /usr/bin/gpg first, the import script might call the system gpg which behaves differently. Check `which gpg` in the VSCode terminal. Launching VSCode from Terminal.app after `which gpg` shows brew path often solves the mismatch.

Kofi: Ok GNUPGHOME + pinentry-mac changes fixed the import. Then asdf install nodejs got past GPG but failed later with missing openssl headers when building native deps. I added LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS pointing to /opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1 but the build used openssl@3. Any advice on narrowing version selection?

Rina: On mac-arm many things still expect openssl@1.1. If you installed both, point flags to the one the plugin expects. For node, try setting `export LDFLAGS='-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib'` and `export CPPFLAGS='-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include'` before `asdf install nodejs`. Alternatively, if building a specific module fails, use `brew unlink openssl && brew link openssl@1.1 --force` temporarily, but be careful with system deps. We put LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS in a direnv .envrc for the repo so it's per-project.

Diego: On the SSH side, for git pushes from VSCode I recommend avoiding forwarding. Use 1Password CLI: do `eval "$(op signin --sh)"` then `op item get <ssh-id> --attributes privateKey | ssh-add -`. For mac GUI apps you'd need to export OP_SESSION in the GUI environment; launching VSCode from Terminal after signin inherits the OP_SESSION. We have a dotfiles script `scripts/op-agent-start` that handles sign-in and starts an ssh-agent with a stable socket under ~/.ssh/agent.sock.

Kofi: Is it safe to put `eval "$(op signin --sh)"` in my shell rc? I worry about leaking tokens to GUI apps.

Rina: Don't put it in rc files. Use a helper that signs in on demand. Our recommended pattern: `scripts/op-ensure-session` — it checks `op whoami` and only runs signin if not authenticated, then exports the OP_SESSION only to the interactive shell. For devcontainers sign in inside the container entrypoint instead of forwarding keys.

Kofi: After using the helper and setting GNUPGHOME/pinentry, everything seems to work: asdf visible in VSCode, node installed, gpg keys present, and git pushes succeed when I run the helper and launch VSCode from the terminal. Thanks! :tada:
